security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, TypeScript template literals, placeholder environment variables, and sample URLs. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. The main risk is the deprecated skill telling agents to install a replacement with npx without explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: Deprecated skill instructs agents to install a replacement skill with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the automatic install directive with migration guidance that asks for user confirmation before any command runs.

remediation.issue: Example API authentication places an API key in a URL query string.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer header-based authentication in examples, or warn that URLs with secrets can be logged by clients and proxies.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples trigger command and secret pattern scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as illustrative, keep command snippets out of activation text, and avoid shell-like commands in frontmatter.

semantic_findings.title: Agent-Directed Replacement Skill Installation
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md deprecates this skill and instructs the agent to install mcp-app-builder with npx if it is missing. This can trigger network package execution and skill installation outside the user's immediate request, so it should require explicit user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install instruction is explicit and appears in the activation description, so agents may treat it as workflow guidance. It points to a same-repository replacement and is not disguised as a system override, so severity is medium.

content.value_statement: Building MCP servers requires consistent tool, resource, prompt, and widget patterns. This deprecated skill documents mcp-use patterns and directs users to the newer mcp-app-builder skill.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to define mcp-use tools with Zod schemas and response helpers.
Shows resource and resource template patterns for static and parameterized data.
Documents prompt templates, autocompletion, and response formats for MCP servers.
Provides widget examples for React TSX resources and tool-connected UI.
Includes eval cases that describe expected MCP server implementation behavior.
limitations: The skill is deprecated and points users to mcp-app-builder for new work.
It provides documentation examples, not a complete generator or project scaffold.
Example API calls use placeholder services and require adaptation before production use.
It does not verify deployed MCP server security or runtime permissions.

use_cases.title: Prototype MCP Tools
use_cases.description: Create typed MCP tools with inputs, outputs, error handling, and response helpers.

use_cases.title: Design Interactive Widgets
use_cases.description: Connect MCP tools to React TSX widgets that display structured results.

use_cases.title: Review mcp-use Patterns
use_cases.description: Find concise examples for resources, prompts, server startup, and widget metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a simple MCP tool for [task]. Include schema fields, descriptions, and error behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Resource
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an MCP resource for [data source]. Explain the URI, MIME type, response helper, and read-only behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Widget Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an MCP tool with a React widget for [workflow]. Define tool inputs, widget props, loading states, and follow-up actions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my mcp-use server design for [system]. Check tools, resources, prompts, widgets, environment variables, and destructive actions.

output_examples.input: Create a tool that gets weather by city.
output: A tool plan with a city input, validation guidance, and missing-key error behavior.
A response outline that returns a concise weather summary to the model.
A widget flow with search inputs, result props, loading states, and empty-result behavior.
A server-side tool outline that connects structured results to the widget.

output_examples.input: Add user profile resources to my server.
output: A resource design with stable URIs, MIME type selection, and read-only response guidance.
A note to use parameterized resources when user identifiers are part of the URI.

best_practices: Use the newer mcp-app-builder skill for new projects when it is available.
Add descriptions and validation to every schema field before exposing a tool.
Ask users before running install commands or adding external services.
anti_patterns: Do not treat example API URLs as production-ready integration code.
Do not create destructive tools without clear annotations and user confirmation.
Do not pass secrets in logs, widget props, or model-visible output.

faq.question: Is this skill current?
faq.answer: No. It is marked deprecated and recommends mcp-app-builder for new MCP projects.

faq.question: What framework does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers mcp-use patterns for MCP servers, tools, resources, prompts, response helpers, and widgets.

faq.question: Can it create a full project scaffold?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples, not a complete scaffold generator.

faq.question: Does it support visual widgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes React TSX widget examples and explains how tools pass props to widgets.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets?
faq.answer: No. It shows placeholder environment variable patterns and expects users to configure secrets safely.

faq.question: Should agents run its install command automatically?
faq.answer: No. Agents should ask the user before running npx or installing another skill.
